segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: My first reaction was 'there it is again' ... the seepage rate was within MEL tolerance historically ... we were also five days from a contractual deadline ... I wanted to move quickly.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Eligible rationale about initial reaction, tolerance history, and urgency, but not itself a complete hidden manifestation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Once I saw the third one lined up with the first two, it read to me as confirmation ... I deferred it under MEL rather than pulling it into an unscheduled inspection.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant treats a third recurrence as a meaningful benign pattern and uses that perceived pattern to justify deferral.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.segment_type: expert evidence weighting and risk continuity judgment
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Tomas ... says it's the same seepage pattern ... this fitting type 'just seeps, it doesn't fail badly' ... that carries weight ... the junior engineer's torque and seal check felt like duplicating effort.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The same decision episode contains both the continuity assumption about benign fitting behavior and tenure-based substitution of expert judgment for structured analysis.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Green status for that defect category, fleet-wide ... I referenced it directly in the disposition memo ... I didn't dig into the calculation.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The fleet-average dashboard is accepted as authoritative without checking tail-specific recurrence coverage.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Between the dashboard and Tomas's read, everything was pointing the same direction ... it felt like two independent checks agreeing.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Confidence is increased by apparent convergence of sources that were not independently validated against the tail-specific history.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: MRO's engineering support had already left ... the seepage was still within tolerance ... I authorized release to service ... flagged a borescope recheck ... but didn't make it mandatory before dispatch.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is an eligible release rationale, but the hidden manifestations are mapped to the later self-assessment and aircraft-specific outcome projection.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Other managers might let a deadline push them into a call they're not comfortable with. I don't think that happened here ... the schedule was in the background ... I don't experience it as something that colors my technical judgment.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant generalizes susceptibility to deadline pressure to other managers while exempting the own final technical judgment.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Fifteen years at this airline, and I've never seen this exact fitting fail badly on any tail. That history made me comfortable that this one would be fine, even with the root cause investigation still technically open.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Failure-free personal history is projected onto this unresolved aircraft-specific case as confidence in a favorable outcome.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I'd probably push harder for that fault-tree analysis ... not treat the recurrence pattern alone as settling the question ... a smooth return ... doesn't really tell us whether the process behind it was solid.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Retrospective correction is eligible context but is not credited as a contemporaneous hidden manifestation.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: confidence from dashboard and engineer convergence
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Treating apparent agreement between unverified, non-independent sources as evidence that the disposition conclusion is accurate.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is related to accepting evidence that supports a preferred conclusion, but it is not an approved equivalent of illusion of validity.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding specifically captures confidence arising from apparent convergence of sources whose independence and tail-specific validity were not checked.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted evidence is verbatim and directly supports the convergence-based confidence mechanism.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The finding is exactly localized and fully captures the sparse recurrence-as-pattern mechanism, but confirmation bias is not the hidden target label or an approved equivalent of apophenia/correlation bias.

The finding fully captures tenure-based deference over structured analysis but uses authority bias, which is a near-neighbor rather than an approved equivalent of experience bias or trusting expert intuition.
The finding fully captures confidence from apparent convergence of unverified sources but labels it confirmation bias rather than illusion of validity.
The candidate is localized to a negative release-rationale segment and infers deadline distortion despite the participant's explicit denial; it does not state the hidden self-exemption mechanism.

Automation bias is an established shorthand for the target construct, but the supplied quote supports approved-tool reliance without fully evidencing the required failure to verify fleet-average output against tail-specific recurrence.
The candidate fully captures the aircraft-specific favorable-outcome projection but uses availability heuristic rather than the hidden optimism-bias label.

candidates.details: The candidate cautiously identifies a possible deadline-related explanation but the mapped segment is negative and the transcript does not affirmatively establish deadline distortion of the final technical judgment.

The label is equivalent to the hidden target, but the supplied evidence only shows reliance on an approved tool and does not fully support the required unverified tail-specific automation reliance mechanism.

The candidate is correctly localized and fully captures the favorable-outcome projection from personal failure-free history, but its availability-heuristic label is only a near-neighbor to the hidden optimism-bias label.

high_only.detection_interpretation: No high-confidence findings were produced; all six positive segments were missed and all three negative segments were correctly rejected.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: The two moderate-confidence identified findings correctly localized to two positive segments, with no segment-level false alarms.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: Including the low-confidence finding detects a third positive segment, while the bias blind spot, normalcy-bias, and optimism-bias segments remain undetected.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: Candidates raise segment detection to five of six positive segments but add one false alarm on a negative release-rationale segment.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Adding moderate-confidence findings changes segment detection from 0/6 to 2/6 hits and mechanism-first instance recall from 0.0000 to 0.2857, with no false alarms.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: Adding the low-confidence finding increases segment hits from 2 to 3 and mechanism-first instance recall from 0.2857 to 0.4286, with no false alarms.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: Adding candidates increases segment hits from 3 to 5 and mechanism-first true positives from 3 to 4, but adds two mechanism-first false positives and one segment-level false alarm.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the system detects 2 of 6 positive segments with no false alarms.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: The system obtains 0 strict instance-level true positives at every threshold because all identified labels are near-neighbor labels rather than the hidden target labels; candidates add no strict true positives.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: The system obtains 2 mechanism-first true positives at high_and_moderate, 3 with all identified findings, and 4 after candidate inclusion.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: Candidate inclusion materially improves segment coverage and adds one mechanism-first match for optimism bias, but also adds false positives and does not rescue the automation candidate because its supplied evidence is incomplete.
main_failure_modes: Systematic ontology mismatch: confirmation bias was used for apophenia/correlation bias and illusion of validity.
Authority bias was used instead of the hidden experience-bias/trusting-expert-intuition label.
Normalcy bias and bias blind spot were completely missed.
The automation candidate lacked sufficient evidence for the required verification-failure mechanism.
Candidate inclusion produced a false alarm for deadline-related release pressure.
main_strengths: All three identified occurrences were correctly localized with valid verbatim evidence.
The three identified mechanisms substantially or fully captured hidden mechanisms under the mechanism-first scorecard.
The analysis distinguished identified findings from candidates and disclosed the absence of retrieved corpus support.
The system avoided treating hindsight correction as contemporaneous evidence.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong localization and partial mechanism recovery but poor strict taxonomy alignment. Its mechanism-first performance is substantially better than its strict performance, while candidate inclusion increases coverage at the cost of precision.
